newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.
newsitem.headline: Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.

text.p: AUSSIE RULES
FOOTBALL PARK: THE COACH'S CURSE.
Call it the curse of Football Park, call it whatever you want, but there is no denying cruel things happen to AFL coaches after a visit there.
Inspirational North Melbourne captain Wayne Schimmelbusch was Football Park's first victim less than two years after he took the reins at Arden St.
Days after a pre-season night game at the ground in 1993 where Adelaide thrashed North by 137 points Schimma was promptly shown the door and replaced by Denis Pagan.
Within two years his rival coach that night Graham Cornes was gone too, swept away by the weight of expectation that goes with the territory in a one team town.
Cornes' replacement Robert Shaw lasted only two years before packing his bags and returning to Melbourne.
With new Adelaide coach Malcolm Blight and Port Adelaide mentor John Cahill performing well this year, the curse of Football Park has again fallen on visiting coaches.
Neil Balme was the first to go after Melbourne fell meekly to Port Adelaide in round nine and this week Richmond coach Robert Walls was sacked days after Adelaide thrashed the Tigers by 137 points.

Walls' position was untenable after he accepted responsibility for an insipid display against Melbourne in round 10. This was despite private and public reassurances from president Leon Daphne that he had full support at board level.
Daphne withdrew his support last Monday.
"It's clearly a change of opinion on my part," he said. "Nothing stands still and footy is a game where performance is the only measurement."
It seems the same standards do not apply to the Richmond Football Club committee which appointed Walls amid much fanfare less than two years ago.

Walls' sacking should come as no surpise because he was Richmond's 10th coach since 1977. What is surprising is that Richmond has never before sacked a coach during the season. Walls now has the distinction of being the only coach sacked during a season on two occasions. Less than two years after guiding Carlton to the 1987 premiership, Walls was replaced by Alex Jesaulenko following a home loss to lowly Brisbane.
Expect a good showing from Richmond when it plays the Western Bulldogs at Optus Oval on Saturday.
Since 1978, 11 coaches have been sacked during the year and under the new coach nine of those teams have won the following week.
However, the Western Bulldogs are coming off three straight losses and should win to keep alive their hopes of a top four finish.
SHEEDY'S ESSENDON EMPIRE
Essendon keeps losing but Kevin Sheedy's position as coach grows stronger by the day.

Now in his 17th season, Sheedy demands, even commands loyalty and he is getting just that from the Essendon committee which is allowing him to restructure the football department to give him complete control of football operations.
Nothing, however, will save the Bombers against North Melbourne at the MCG tonight.
In Saturday's matches, Sydney will thrash Melbourne at the MCG, Geelong will be too strong for Port Adlaide at Kardinia Park and Brisbane will pummel Hawthorn at the Gabba.

On Sunday, Adelaide will hammer Carlton at Football Park and sour celebrations for Stephen Kernahan, who becomes the game's longest serving captain. St Kilda will be untroubled by Collingwood at Waverley Park and, in Perth's local derby, West Coast should make it six wins to nothing over Fremantle at Subiaco Oval.
*Andrew Bartram will be writing a regular AFL column for Reuters. Any feedback to michael.stapleton@reuters.com
